newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks shadow Wall Street, pare losses.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks shadow Wall Street, pare losses.

text.p: Mexican stocks partly recovered from earlier losses to close almost flat Thursday, following the lead of the Dow Jones industrial average and amid some bargain-hunting, analysts and traders said.
"The bourse was basically influenced by the Dow Jones which was hurt by the increase in long bond yields," said Roberto Galvan, an analyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
The blue-chip IPC index ended off 1.57 points, or 0.05 percent, at 3,359.46. Volume was light at 36.5 million shares.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 5.78 at 6,442.49, after earlier dropping as much as 96 points. On Tuesday, the day before the Christmas holiday, the Dow fell 101 points.
"Lack of players was the main feature of the session. We saw little activity and pared losses when some bottom-fishing buyers stepped in," a desk trader said.
On the broad market, 83 stocks changed hands, and losers trounced winners by 50 to 14.
Traders noted that many share prices fell after gaining prior to the close of 1996 for portfolio evaluation purposes.
"Most falls were natural adjustments after many wished to raise prices for portfolios," a trader said.
Tourist operator Situr headed the sliders' list, off three centavos (1 cent) to 40 centavos (5 cents).
Traders meanwhile said some share prices increased on speculative buying ahead of expected gains next week, rather than any sectoral or fundamental trend.
Mining stock Grupo Mexico topped the gainers, up 1.20 pesos (15 cents) to 25.60 pesos ($3.24).
Another analyst said Mexican stocks were still in a consolidation phase while gathering strength for another attempt to crack the 3,400-point barrier.
"We were expecting trade to be slack in the holiday period, but prices should begin to climb again next week," he said.
